ev.q: During July 2000--June 2001, an estimated 4.3 million (95% CI=3.7--4.8 million) sports- and recreation-related injuries were treated
Rates were highest among persons aged 10--14 years (75.4 for boys, 36.3 for girls)
The overall rate of sports- and recreation-related injuries was 15.4 per 1,000 population
Overall, 2.3% (95% CI=1.5%--3.0%) of persons with sports- and recreation-related injuries were hospitalized.
The overall rate of sports- and recreation-related injuries was 15.4 per 1,000 population
Among all ages, rates were higher for males than for females
The percentage of all unintentional injury-related ED visits that were sports- and recreation-related was highest for persons aged 10--14 years
NEISS-AIP provides data on approximately 500,000 injury- and consumer product--related ED cases each year.
NEISS-AIP is designed to provide national estimates but not state or local estimates.

methods_quotes.q: Confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated by using a direct variance estimation procedure that accounted for the sample weights and complex sample design.
Each case was assigned a sample weight based on the inverse probability of selection; these weights were added to provide national estimates
Rates were calculated by using averaged 2000--2001 U.S. Census Bureau population data.
